claims.text: Laser surface alloying with aluminum will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy lacks an intrinsically stable protective oxide scale.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy rapidly oxidizes under extreme-temperature conditions.
Laser surface alloying will produce a surface layer with substantially increased aluminum concentration.
The aluminum-enriched surface will foster formation of a dense, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 film.
Heating the aluminum-enriched layer in an oxidizing environment promotes formation of thermodynamically stable Al2O3.
The resulting Al2O3 scale acts as a barrier to further oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion will reduce oxide-scale growth and substrate degradation.
Laser-alloyed samples will have lower mass gain and oxide-scale growth than untreated samples under identical conditions.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys form non-protective oxide scales that cause rapid oxidation and degradation at high temperatures.
The proposed improvement should occur in ambient air at 1100–1200 degrees Celsius for exposures lasting 24–100 hours.
The benefit is limited to the specified high-temperature oxidizing conditions and may not persist at lower temperatures or in non-oxidizing atmospheres.
A reduction in mass gain of more than approximately 20% is the proposed threshold for a significant improvement.
